errors.english: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body, born from a hundred merits.
errors.why: The quoted line first says the Tathāgata's body is born from all the white (virtuous) dharmas; this is dropped.

fix.find: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body, born from a hundred merits.
fix.replace: the body of the (Tathagata) One Thus Gone, born from all virtuous qualities, is the (Dharmakaya) Truth Body, born from a hundred merits.

errors.english: Because they are the essential nature of what should and should not be done
errors.why: The Tibetan says they are 'karma' because they are by nature acting and refraining (action and non-action), not 'what should and should not be done'; the 'they are karma' half of the karmapatha etymology is also lost.

note: Accurate rendering of the faith instructions apart from one dropped phrase in the quoted line on the Tathāgata's body and a loose gloss on karmapatha.

errors.english: The actions of the Supreme Sage
errors.why: MMK 17.2 says the Supreme Sage taught that actions are intention and the intended; they are not the Sage's own actions (the genitive here stands for the agentive).

note: A sound rendering of Avalokitavrata on MMK 17.2–3; the cetanā/cetayitvā distinction and the ṛṣi etymology are handled correctly.

errors.english: The opponent asserts that the meaning of this reason is unproven in any sense.
errors.why: གང་ཡང་རུང་བ་ལ་མ་གྲུབ་པ is the technical fallacy anyatarāsiddha, unproven for one of the two parties, not 'unproven in any sense'.

fix.replace: unproven for one of the two parties (anyatarāsiddha)

errors.english: the subject characterized as "otherness" depends upon something else
errors.why: The subject called 'other' depends on otherness (the Vaiśeṣika category) itself, not on 'something else'.

errors.english: the viewer is not other than the object of viewing
errors.why: ལྟ་བ is seeing (darśana), distinct from the seer (ལྟ་བ་པོ, mentioned separately in the context); the English uses 'viewer' throughout.

note: The argument's overall shape is kept, but the fallacy term and the seeing/seer triad are mishandled.

errors.english: If words were to engage strictly with the ultimate truth, then the words for the objects of other philosophical views would not engage without a cause.
errors.why: The summary verses are turned into prose, and རྒྱུ་མེད་ཅན (baseless) describes the objects of other views; the verse does not mean the words engage 'without a cause'.

note: The PVSV-commentary argument on word-objects and pradhāna is broadly faithful; the summary verses were flattened into prose.

span_why: The English is a single vacuous sentence; none of the side (conceptual cognition appearing as grasping a real thing, the opponent on external particulars, the answer about vyavahartṛs) is translated.
note: Not a translation of this side.

errors.english: When the mind engages with an entity [note: original: "vastu"], it produces an incompatible cause
errors.why: It is the cognition of non-entity that, by producing an incompatible cause in the form of vāsanā, cuts the continuum of the very cognition of an entity; the English makes the entity-cognition the producer.

errors.english: just as heat is distinct from cold
errors.why: The simile is cold [removed] by fire, an image of one thing eliminating another, not 'heat being distinct from cold'.

errors.english: one should conceptualize the nature of impermanence and so forth
errors.why: The honorific མཛད states that he (the Teacher) examines its nature as impermanent and so on; it is not an injunction to 'one'.

note: The argument on the mutual exclusion of the two conceptions is hard to follow because several agents and similes are misread.
A faithful rendering of the defence of Mahāyāna as buddhavacana, including the patriarchal transmission list and the parity argument.

errors.english: **except for those where it was not said, 'I will see if it is built or finished by the benefactor.'**
errors.why: The offence applies to one who has NOT said 'Look whether the donor has built or finished it' (the next sentence says that saying it is no fault); 'except for' inverts this.

fix.find: **except for those where it was not said, 'I will see if it is built or finished by the benefactor.'**
fix.replace: **for one who has not said, 'Look whether the benefactor has built or finished it.'**

errors.english: There is no downfall if they cover it with flat boards.
errors.why: སྤང་ལེབ are slabs of turf or sod; the wooden planks are the separate ཤིང་ལེབ case.

note: The Vinaya commentary on the building rule is mostly clear, but the key exemption clause is inverted.

errors.why: The Tibetan says that mentioning 'ascertained' is NOT superfluous, which is the thesis the whole passage then defends.

note: A sound exposition of anvaya/vyatireka and the śyāma example, but the opening sentence states the opposite of the thesis.

errors.english: The cause may exist without the effect, so the answer to "non-observation does not establish the non-existence of the object" is also fully stated.
errors.why: 'A cause may exist without its effect' is part of the opponent's objection being answered; the English presents it as the author's own premise.

fix.find: The cause may exist without the effect, so the answer to "non-observation does not establish the non-existence of the object" is also fully stated.
fix.replace: This also answers the objection: "Since a cause may exist without its effect, non-observation does not establish the non-existence of the object."

errors.english: their reversal is the non-existence of non-observation
errors.why: Their absence is non-existence established by non-observation, not 'the non-existence of non-observation'.

note: A literal rendering of the anupalabdhi discussion that misplaces the objection and blurs the key formulation of non-existence.
